paper_metadata.title: Quantum Option Proﬁt and Loss Encoding for Risk Assessment

experiments.description: QOPLE loading, payoff mapping, and cumulative PnL construction for a European call option using three sampling qubits, with strike-price encoding and threshold comparison shown in circuit figures.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Option Profit and Loss Encoding (QOPLE) with L-P-V circuit construction

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Option expiration price distribution is truncated to three standard deviations around the mean and discretized into 2^n samples; n qubits encode the price distribution. The strike price K is encoded in a separate k-qubit register, and a control qubit marks whether ST <= K. The V operator compares PnL against threshold l using a controlled comparator.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Construct the cumulative distribution function P[PT <= l] for option profit and loss, where PT = max(ST - K, 0) for a call option.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Controlled comparison and conditional flipping of ancilla qubits; no penalty formulation.

problem_instance.description: European call option under the Black-Scholes-Merton model, with one detailed instance shown for S0 = 2.0, sigma = 0.4, T = 40/365, r = 0.05, K = 1.896.

dataset_specification.description: Underlying asset price ST follows a lognormal distribution from the BSM model; distribution truncated to [ST_min, ST_max] within three standard deviations and uniformly sampled into 2^n points.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Truncate lognormal distribution to three standard deviations around the mean; equidistant sampling of ST; fit relation ST = 0.229 * i + 1.209 for n = 3.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Circuit-level simulation and visualization in Qiskit; probability under each l value measured three times and averaged.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Load lognormal option-price distribution; compute payoff PT and cumulative PnL thresholding.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Average three probability estimates for each l value; compare quantum CDF against Monte Carlo baseline.

experiments.description: Scalability study of QOPLE/QORA for two European call option instances across different sampling-qubit counts, comparing quantum VaR estimates to classical Monte Carlo.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Option Risk Assessment (QORA) using QOPLE plus maximum-likelihood-based amplitude estimation and binary search VaR

problem_formulation.encoding_details: European call option price distribution loaded into n qubits; strike price encoded in k qubits; P operator maps payoff; V operator encodes cumulative PnL below threshold l; binary search over l to find VaR satisfying P[PT <= l] >= alpha.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate option Value at Risk (VaR) as the minimum loss threshold l such that P[PT <= l] >= alpha.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Binary search over payoff threshold l; controlled comparator and ancilla-based target-state marking.

problem_instance.description: Two European call option instances with different strike prices; one detailed instance uses S0 = 2.0, sigma = 0.4, T = 40/365, r = 0.05, K = 1.896; the second uses K = 1.5. Both are evaluated at alpha = 0.95.

dataset_specification.description: BSM lognormal underlying price distribution; truncated to three standard deviations around the mean; discretized into 2^n samples; one case uses fit ST = 0.229 * i + 1.209 and payoff PT = 0.229 * i - 0.687 for i > iK.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Uniform sampling of ST over truncated interval; encode strike price K as integer iK; evaluate VaR by binary search over l.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Simulation in Qiskit; compare quantum VaR estimates against classical Monte Carlo with 10,000 repeated samples; relative error reported versus classical result; probability at each l measured three times and averaged.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Construct option price distribution, payoff mapping, and binary search bounds lmin/lmax.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compute VaR baseline with 10000 Monte Carlo samples; compute relative error between quantum and classical VaR.

speedup_claims.conditions: for estimating VaR / target-state probability with the same precision; in the QAE-style amplitude-estimation setting
speedup_claims.caveats: Claim is theoretical; actual simulations are on Qiskit and the paper does not report wall-clock runtime. The MLE variant is presented as reducing resource usage while retaining the quadratic advantage.

scalability_data.metric_value: within 1% relative error versus classical Monte Carlo

experiments.description: Comparison of QAE-style amplitude estimation versus the paper's MLE-based amplitude estimation on the same option-risk setup, including CDF and VaR estimation at n = 4 qubits.

algorithm.variant: Maximum-likelihood estimation (MLE) amplitude estimation versus traditional QAE

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Same QOPLE encoding of option price distribution and payoff as in the main model; target qubit amplitude corresponds to P[PT <= l].
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate the amplitude/probability of the target state and derive VaR via binary search.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Grover-style amplitude amplification followed by MLE post-processing; binary search over l.

problem_instance.description: European call option instance consistent with Fig. 5, discretized to four qubits; compared under QAE and MLE for cumulative PnL and VaR estimation.

dataset_specification.description: BSM-based synthetic option distribution; same option parameterization as the main example.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Discretize option distribution to n = 4 qubits; evaluate CDF of PT under different amplification counts.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Simulation comparison of QAE and MLE outputs; VaR estimated by final dichotomy; classical Monte Carlo with 10000 samples used as reference.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Prepare the same option distribution and thresholding problem for both QAE and MLE comparisons.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compare estimated amplitudes/CDFs and VaR against Monte Carlo baseline; assess error behavior and resource savings.

results.unit: % (at n=7 in the broader study; referenced in comparison discussion)

speedup_claims.factor: quadratic speedup, O(1/M) error convergence vs O(1/sqrt(M)) classical Monte Carlo
speedup_claims.conditions: amplitude estimation setting; same target-state probability precision
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states MLE retains the quadratic advantage of QAE while reducing auxiliary qubits and controlled operations; no runtime benchmark is reported.

speedup_claims.factor: at least 15% fewer ancillary qubits and 3x fewer controlled amplification operations
speedup_claims.conditions: for the compared option-risk setup with m in {2,3,4,5} and MLE amplification sequence {0,1,2}
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper does not provide the exact absolute qubit counts in the comparison table, only the relative reduction.
